cases.root_cause: The three pre-open option snapshot runs on 2026-10-15 (09:14:48–09:20:21) all failed within 4–16 s on connection/underlying-quote errors rather than on any run-budget or secdef problem: the first died with 'SPX: no spot price', and the two that followed failed to connect at all (Socket disconnect, then TimeoutError in 4 s). There is no run-level IBKR farm code (1100/2103/2105/2157) or 354/10089-series code recorded for these failures, so the data does not distinguish between a short Gateway/farm outage of the underlying quote (gateway runbook sections A/C/D) and a transient reconnect. Notably, coverage for the session was still 100 % (78/78 slots) — the pre-open slots are outside the RTH SLI — and the next runs succeeded, so no snapshot history was lost; only SLI 2 timeliness for the day fell to 89.74 %.

Alpaca returned the 2026-10-15 bars late/incompletely during the session: intraday equity_bars runs from 10:20 ET onward completed normally but consistently reported missing_bars (rising from ~100 to 700 bars of 3,900), then the 17:30 ET eod refetch re-pulled 2026-10-15 and recovered every missing bar (3,900 rows, missing_bars 0). No data is lost; the missing bars were a vendor-side gap/lag that the vendor later filled, not a failure on our side.

The IB Gateway's API port was not accepting connections at 09:10:02 ET, so both the option_snapshots and index_snapshots runs failed their connect after 4 s with TimeoutError() — the exact pattern runbooks/stale-snapshots maps to "Options and indices failing, TimeoutError() after ~4 s" → gateway.md section A. The Gateway was unreachable at least from the 09:10 slot (option run already had a 62,101 s = ~17.3 h gap since the prior successful run, i.e. since the 15:55 ET close of 2026-10-15), and it stayed unavailable long enough that the next option run at 09:40:00 ET still failed/first recovering success is the 10:05-ish catch-up; service was restored by the 10:09:43 ET retry, and from 10:20 onward option/index snapshots succeeded normally. Cause of the freeze itself (wedged Gateway vs restart/login) is not established by pipeline_runs alone — the Gateway log and `pit.health gateway` output are needed, hence medium confidence.

A single Alpaca HTTP call dropped mid-response: the 13:55 UTC equity_bars slot failed at 10:09:43 ET after 18 s with RemoteProtocolError('Server disconnected without sending a response.') — a transient vendor-side disconnect, not a config or subscription problem. The pipeline self-recovered: the EOD run at 17:30 ET refetched the last 10 sessions with missing_bars = 0, and session completeness (SLI-3) is 100%, so no bars were lost and no action is needed.

The 09:20 option snapshot run hit exactly the 480 s (8 min) execution timeout and was killed, so Airflow recorded status "failed" with an empty error field — a hang, not an exception. The evidence points to a single hung IBKR request: the run never produced chain_errors or partial rows, index snapshots in the same slot succeeded in ~4 s (Gateway connect fine), and the next option run at 09:25 started on time and succeeded within its budget. The data does not pin down which request hung, so the cause below is the best-supported pattern, not proven.

Codes 10090 and 10167 are IBKR market-data permission messages, not connectivity faults: per runbooks/gateway section C, 10090 means "not subscribed for this instrument" and 10167 means IBKR served delayed data instead of live for that request. On 2026-10-19 they recurred on the option snapshot runs through the session (at least 09:38 through 15:50 ET) while the same slots succeeded and the SLIs stayed green, so this looks like the collector user not covering a subset of the requested instruments/session, not a Gateway or farm outage — collection itself worked.

Neither session was lost: the 0% on 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 is a monitoring artefact. The option-snapshot runs for those days were collected on the Mac host and are not recorded in this host's pipeline_runs (get_runs returns "no runs recorded" for both days), while ops/slo.md's own table shows 10-22 at 100% and 10-23 at 100% coverage (10-23: secdef stall, 4 slots late, no slot lost). The 17:30 eod refetch on 10-27 did reconfirm the days happened (equity_bars 3900 rows each). By contrast, the 2026-10-26 0% is a real loss (Gateway frozen all session, 0/78 slots).

IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) server stopped answering for ~5 minutes on 2026-10-23: every option and index run first had to call qualifyContracts/reqSecDefOptParams, so the requests hung. The index task was killed by its 2-min timeout on both attempts, losing the 10:35 index snapshot; the option run burned its whole 6-min budget on the hung first chain (RequestTimeout = 300 s), failed, and its retry plus the single-slot queue (max_active_runs=1) pushed the following four option slots 3.5–5.5 min late. Market data (quotes, farms) was not at fault.

The morning contract_cache refresh (bulk re-listing of ~55 expiries) overloaded IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) service and the IB Gateway froze. From 09:16 ET the Gateway's API port accepted no connections, IBC's RESTART could not fix it (its UI was wedged too), and only a container restart with a full phone-2FA login at 19:40 ET brought it back, so all 78 regular-hours option snapshot slots were lost with no backfill.

The two days are not attributable to the same cause on the evidence available. On 2026-10-27 the 09:10 slot was the only failure of the day (78/78 option slots OK, SLI1 100%): both option_snapshots and index_snapshots failed on the same scheduled run id with a bare TimeoutError() after 4 s, matching the stale-snapshots runbook row for a Gateway API that briefly refused connections at the 09:10 pre-open slot, and collection self-recovered at the next slot. On 2026-10-30 the same 09:10:01 run id failed both datasets with an identical 4 s TimeoutError() and no ibkr_error_codes, but index_snapshots shows a 62,095 s (≈17.2 h) gap and option_snapshots a 61,881 s (≈17.2 h) gap, i.e. no successful IBKR snapshot of either kind anywhere before 09:10 that day. A same-day morning Gateway stall is plausible but not proven, and the known 10-28 → 11-02 morning secdef-stall recurrence explicitly ends at 11-02, so it does not cover 10-30; calling both the same cause would be an inference the data doesn't support.

A routine IBKR connectivity blip that healed itself within the same run: no option snapshots run on 2026-11-05 failed, every 5-minute slot succeeded with quotes, and the day's SLIs are fully met — so no option data was lost and no action is needed.

No fault to fix: the 2157 and 2103 codes are IBKR data-farm drops that recovered by themselves within the same run. Every option run on 2026-11-11 is a success (0 failed of 82, including the 14:30 run that logged code 2103), quotes kept flowing in the affected runs, and the SLOs are met on 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11 (100% option coverage, 98.72% on-time). Per runbooks/gateway section D such farm blips are routine and not alerted; no RECONNECTDATA or restart is warranted. One caveat: I could not independently verify the recurring 2157 around 10:30/11:30 in the morning, because get_runs truncates the 82-run day and returned only the afternoon; that is inferred from the operator's report and the pattern of the 14:30 run.

The IB Gateway's API port stopped accepting connections just before the 09:10 slot, so the 09:10, 09:15 and 09:25 option slot attempts and the 09:10/09:15 index attempts each died in their connect with TimeoutError() after ~4-5 s (the signature the gateway runbook section A / stale-snapshots "By cause" table gives for "Gateway API not accepting connections"), followed by one run whose chains failed with ConnectionError('Socket disconnect' / 'Not connected') and codes 2104/2106/2119/2158. The failed slots were then started late in a short catch-up burst at 09:25:15-09:26:03. The Gateway recovered by itself: the session finished with 78/78 option slots covered (SLI1 100%, SLI2 98.72%), so this was a self-limiting episode, not a wedged Gateway; the runs data alone does not pin down what made the port unreachable (no 2FA/restart evidence, no secdef-stall evidence like the long 6-min hangs in incidents/2026-10-23).

The data volume is full: from ~13:05 ET every collection task (option_snapshots, index_snapshots, equity_bars, and the 17:30 daily_bars/corporate_actions/assets runs) dies within ~2 s with OSError(28, 'No space left on device'). This is not a Gateway or vendor problem — the Gateway was healthy and all datasets had been succeeding minutes earlier.

The nightly `dbt build` in the `eod` DAG could not take the write lock on /opt/airflow/data/curated.duckdb because another Python process (PID 4127) already held an open handle (DuckDB allows one process per file, even a read-only handle blocks dbt). Collection itself is unaffected: the collectors write raw/staged Parquet, not DuckDB.

Every Alpaca call on 2026-11-12 is rejected with HTTP 401 Unauthorized, so all equity_bars runs failed in ~1 s each and no bars were collected; the Alpaca API key/credentials are invalid or expired. The IB Gateway side is healthy (option and index snapshots succeeded all session), so this is a vendor auth problem, not a Gateway or pipeline issue. The same 401 also broke daily_bars at the 17:30 EOD run.

Not a Gateway fault and not a subscription gap: the runs succeed and IBKR answers, but every run from at least 13:40 ET onward carries IBKR error 10197 ("live data held by another session of the same user"), so only delayed/no quotes come back. A second session is logged in as the collector's IBKR username and is taking the live market data, leaving option (and index) snapshots with two_sided=0, ask_only=0, bid_only=0 and no_quote=3400 per run. No farm codes (1100/2103/2105/2157) appear, so reconnect_market_data would not help and is not proposed.

Nothing ran on 2026-11-12: there are no pipeline_runs rows at all — not just option/index snapshots but also Alpaca equity bars, daily bars, corporate actions and assets, plus no Gateway check cards (those cards come from the same Airflow host). The stack (host/Docker/Airflow) was not up that day; every scheduled slot was skipped. This is not the IB Gateway incident pattern: at 2026-11-10 09:25–09:26 errors are connection codes 2104/2106/2119/2158 (reconnect notices, not 1100/2103/2157 disconnects), and the SLO data shows 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11 with 78/78 option slots and 3900/3900 bars each, so the Gateway and Alpaca were healthy on the surrounding days. No runs on 11-12 means no failed runs, so there is no IBKR/Alpaca error to chase — consistent with the host or Airflow being down rather than a Gateway fault. Note I can only see this host's pipeline_runs; if collection was moved to another machine I can't tell, so confidence is medium.

IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) service stalled during the pre-open window: the 08:20 Gateway check connected and was logged in but `合约查询` (qualifyContracts) got no answer within 20 s, and the option runs that then started hung on their first request until the 300 s RequestTimeout raised `TimeoutError()` — one hung request consumed the whole 6-min run budget, so `spx_weekly` was "skipped: run budget used up" and every chain failed. Index snapshots failed the same way (no answer, killed by their 2-min timeout). No data-farm codes (2103/2105/2157) or subscription codes appear on these runs, and quotes were flowing normally before and after, so this is a secdef stall, not a Gateway freeze or farm loss: the stall cleared and option/index collection resumed, and the Gateway was not wedged.

Between 11:00 and 11:25 ET, six consecutive option_snapshot runs each ran to exactly 480 s and failed with no error text, i.e. they were killed by the 8-minute option execution timeout (the 6-min run budget being used up), not rejected by a connect error. Only option snapshots were affected: index snapshots succeeded throughout (4–5 s runs, 0 failures all day) and equity bars had 0 failures, so the Gateway API was accepting connections and serving quotes. The runs carry no ibkr_error_codes and no error message, so the data does not show which request consumed each run's budget or why — it could be a slow/hung request (runbook gateway.md A–B) or runs simply too slow for their budget. No single cause is supported by the evidence.

For 25 minutes (13:00–13:25 ET) the SPX market-data farm was disconnected on the IB Gateway (codes 2103 + 2105), so no SPX spot price arrived and every option_snapshots run failed on underlyings lacking a spot price. The collector's own automatic RECONNECTDATA at each run ("sent RECONNECTDATA (OK)") did not clear it. The Gateway itself was not wedged: the API accepted connections (runs failed in 25 s, not a connect TimeoutError) and collection resumed on its own — the 13:30 success carried a residual 2103 that recovered within the run (routine per runbook section D), and 13:35 onward ran clean with no error codes. No index_snapshots runs are recorded for 2026-11-12, so that dataset's state is unknown, not confirmed healthy. Cost is bounded: 6 lost 5-min option slots (non-backfillable) and coverage for the session 72/78 = 92.31% (SLI1 98.46% over 5 sessions, below the 99% objective).

IB Gateway was not serving the API because it was still in its login/2FA phase. "Second Factor Authentication initiated" at 08:58 with "Login has completed" only at 10:17 matches the failure window exactly: every option and index snapshot run from 09:10:01 to 10:15:00 failed its connect in ~4 s with TimeoutError(), and collection resumed with the 10:20 slot once the login completed. This is a gateway restarting/logging-in state (2FA push awaited), not a wedged Gateway: it recovered by itself as soon as the login completed, with no container restart and no data-farm codes in the failing runs.

Not lost. The missing equity bars are a feed problem inside Alpaca's data, not a failed collector: all 90 equity_bars runs on 2026-11-12 succeeded with no API errors, but Alpaca returned nothing for the 12:45+ window; the 17:30 eod refetch did not recover it. Follow the stale-snapshots runbook (SLI 3 / Alpaca branch): check the Alpaca health and, since the refetch did not fix it, backfill the gap by hand. Separately, the 450 missing_bars reported on every run (including clean sessions like 2026-10-29 → 10-30) is a constant baseline, i.e. a reporting artifact rather than today's gap.

The 11:00 option_snapshots run lost IBKR connectivity mid-run (error codes 1100 then 1102 "data maintained" on the same session) and hit its 6-min budget: it timed out with TimeoutError() at 11:05 after 300 s with no rows. With max_active_runs=1 and no retries on snapshot tasks, slots 11:05–11:30 started only as each previous ~5-min run finished, so they ran late. The Gateway itself was fine: index snapshots kept succeeding (4–5 s) throughout, consistent with a transient reconnect (no action needed) rather than a frozen Gateway.
